articles.title: Proactively responding to fluctuations and realizing double-digit growth targets. - Vietnam.vn
articles.summary: Proactively responding to fluctuations and realizing double-digit growth targets.  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
GDP growth in the first nine months reached 9.01%, creating a positive foundation for Vietnam to achieve its double-digit growth target, but comprehensive solutions are still needed, with a priority on macroeconomic stability.
Many positive results have laid the foundation for growth.
The Vietnamese economy in the first nine months of 2026 showed many positive signs, with GDP growth reaching 9.01%, the highest in the past 15 years. Notably, growth showed an improving trend each quarter, with the third quarter reaching 9.95%, indicating the recovery and expansion of production and business activities.
According to data released at the forum "Businesses Facing Exchange Rate, Interest Rate and Energy Price Fluctuations: Response Scenarios for the End of 2026, Prospects for 2027," chaired by the Vietnam Chamber of Commerce and Industry (VCCI) in coordination with the Central Policy and Strategy Committee, held on the afternoon of October 30th in Hanoi , many key economic indicators continued to maintain positive growth.
Tìm hiểu lịch sử
Specifically, the industrial production index for the first nine months increased by 12.3%, the highest since 2019. Total retail sales of goods and consumer service revenue increased by 13.4%, reflecting the expansion of the domestic market. Foreign investment attraction continued to be a bright spot. Registered FDI capital reached US$50.36 billion, an increase of 76.4% compared to the same period last year; implemented FDI capital reached US$21.07 billion, an increase of 12.1%. This is a positive signal for the prospects of investment, production, and the development of Vietnam's export capacity. Export activities maintained their growth momentum, with export turnover increasing by 24.5% in the first nine months. The processing and manufacturing industry continued to play a crucial role in growth and attracting investment capital.
Tìm hiểu lịch sử
At the Forum, experts noted that the results achieved in the first nine months have created a favorable foundation for Vietnam to continue striving to achieve a GDP growth target of 10% or more in 2026.
Specifically, according to Dr. Nguyen Duc Hien, Deputy Head of the Central Policy and Strategy Committee, the Vietnamese economy is undergoing significant changes in its growth model, shifting from reliance on expanding resources to improving the quality and efficiency of resource utilization. Key shifts to focus on include moving from recovery to expanding production; from stimulating demand to creating supply capacity; from oriented growth to integrating technology into growth; and simultaneously enhancing the role of the business sector and improving institutional quality.
However, the positive results of the first nine months do not necessarily mean that the double-digit growth target has been secured. According to economic experts, to achieve a 10% GDP growth rate for the whole year, the fourth quarter needs to achieve a growth rate of over 12.5%. This is a very high requirement, demanding a surge in economic activity in the remaining months of the year.
You may also like
Energy price trends and the challenge of double-digit growth.
Despite positive results, Vietnam's economic outlook for the remaining months of 2026 remains affected by many unpredictable variables in the global economy. Associate Professor Bui Quang Tuan, Vice President of the Vietnam Economic Science Association and former Director of the Vietnam Institute of Economics, commented: The global economy is facing risks from geopolitics , energy prices, monetary policy, and trade fragmentation.
According to Mr. Bui Quang Tuan, global economic growth in 2026 is projected at 3.1%, before recovering to 3.4% in 2027. However, this outlook depends significantly on the evolution of geopolitical conflicts, the possibility of normalizing energy transportation routes, and the monetary policy trends of major economies.
In particular, energy price volatility is becoming one of the notable challenges to growth prospects. Tensions in the Middle East, especially disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, are putting pressure on oil prices, international shipping costs, and insurance.
For Vietnam, rising energy prices can increase input costs for businesses, putting pressure on commodity prices, inflation, and the competitiveness of exports. This necessitates proactive measures to ensure energy supply, control production costs, and limit the impact on economic growth.
Notably, Associate Professor Bui Quang Tuan argues that while Vietnam has positive growth momentum, the room for policy management is narrowing. Promoting high growth must simultaneously ensure macroeconomic stability, control inflation, and maintain the major balances of the economy.
From a business perspective, VCCI Vice President Nguyen Quang Vinh emphasized that fluctuations in exchange rates, interest rates, and energy prices directly impact each contract, order, and investment decision, affecting import costs, debt repayment obligations, capital costs, operations, and the competitiveness of businesses. In this context, businesses need to develop multiple response scenarios instead of relying on a single forecast, while proactively controlling cash flow, capital structure, inventory, and payment terms. In particular, risk management must become a regular part of the decision-making process.
Sharing the same view, according to Dr. Nguyen Duc Hien, to achieve high growth targets, it is first necessary to accelerate the implementation of programs and projects, especially those that can be completed and put into use in the fourth quarter. At the same time, it is necessary to remove bottlenecks related to institutions, land, electricity, infrastructure connectivity, and investment procedures. Furthermore, it is essential to transform resources into tangible results, improve the efficiency of public investment disbursement, promote private investment, and leverage the role of the FDI sector in the processing and manufacturing industries.
You may also like
Mr. Nguyen Duc Hien also noted the need to increase domestic added value, increase the localization rate, and improve productivity. These are important factors for shifting from growth based on scale expansion to growth based on efficiency and competitiveness.
Another issue raised by experts is ensuring a balance between growth targets and macroeconomic stability. Fiscal and monetary policies need to be managed harmoniously, closely monitoring developments in CPI, exchange rates, liquidity, and credit risk; and focusing resources on areas capable of generating real added value.
Associate Professor Bui Quang Tuan suggested that it is necessary to proactively develop policy scenarios in response to fluctuations in the global economy, especially oil prices, international interest rates, and trade. At the same time, it is crucial to strengthen energy security, attract high-quality FDI, diversify export markets, and promote digital transformation and green transformation.
Regarding capital sources, the VCCI representative suggested that, in addition to bank credit, it is necessary to develop a comprehensive capital market and other financial instruments to meet the medium- and long-term capital needs of businesses. Businesses themselves must also improve the quality of governance, ensure transparency in financial reporting, and standardize information to improve their access to capital.
Achieving double-digit growth in 2026 remains a challenge, but the results achieved in the first nine months have laid an important foundation for Vietnam to reach its target.

Osaka Prefecture and Osaka City will exhibit at Singapore FinTech Festival (SFF) 2026, taking place in Singapore from November 18 to 20, 2026, together with two Osaka-based companies selected through an open call.
Osaka and the wider Kansai region form an economic area with a population of approximately 20 million. As one of Japan’s leading business hubs, the region is home to a diverse range of industries, including manufacturing, life sciences, commerce and services.
Through this exhibition, Osaka aims to showcase its business environment and market appeal to overseas companies and investors, creating new partnerships that lead to investment and business expansion in Osaka, as well as collaboration with Osaka-based companies.
Showcasing Osaka at One of the World’s Largest Fintech Events
Singapore FinTech Festival is one of the world’s largest fintech events, bringing together more than 70,000 participants from over 140 countries, including representatives of financial institutions, investors, fintech companies, technology companies and policymakers.
Osaka Prefecture and Osaka City will host a booth within the Japan Pavilion, showcasing Osaka’s business environment and investment opportunities through pitch sessions, business meetings and networking.  It is necessary to facilitate the flow of international capital into Vietnam.
 In an interview with the World and Vietnam Newspaper on the sidelines of the Autumn Economic Forum 2026, Brook Colin Taylor, CEO of VinaCapital International Partners, stated that VIFC-HCMC will play a particularly important role in connecting international capital with projects in Vietnam.
 According to him, Vietnam needs approximately US$1.4 trillion in investment capital to realize its medium- and long-term growth targets. This capital cannot rely solely on the domestic market but needs to be mobilized from abroad, thus requiring an effective mechanism to support international capital flows. VIFC-HCMC plays a crucial role in facilitating this process.
 The CEO of VinaCapital International Partners Co., Ltd. emphasized that international investors are not only interested in investment opportunities but also need a sufficiently transparent and simple environment, with familiar rules, regulations, and laws so that they can quickly implement investment activities. In addition, investors need mechanisms that allow capital flows into and out of Vietnam smoothly, a fast licensing process with minimal delays, and a supportive ecosystem of financial institutions, including banks, securities companies, and asset management companies.
 Regarding the prospects of VIFC-HCMC over the next five years, Mr. Brook Colin Taylor commented that realistic goals need to be set, focusing on building the initial foundation and demonstrating the center's ability to contribute to Vietnam's economic growth. One of the desired outcomes is the presence of several large financial institutions such as banks, asset management companies, and securities firms in Ho Chi Minh City within the VIFC framework.
 Furthermore, he expects VIFC to be able to record successful projects, attract investment capital, implement investments effectively, and facilitate the flow of capital back abroad. According to him, success lies not only in bringing capital into Vietnam but also in ensuring the ability to ensure the flow of capital can move in both directions. If this is proven in the first five years, VIFC-HCMC will have a basis to attract more capital in the following 5-10 years.
 Regarding prioritized investment products, Brook Colin Taylor suggested focusing on relatively simple areas, including private equity, private credit, infrastructure financing, and green finance. He believes these are areas where Vietnam has a high demand and the potential to attract foreign capital.

Through its participation in VIFC-HCMC, the company hopes to collaborate closely with government agencies and business partners to promote Vietnam's economic growth.
 In that spirit, Keppel aims to build investment platforms to bring together investors interested in the Vietnamese market, while also promoting business activities. According to Mr. Joseph Low, these platforms could raise up to $1 billion in investment capital. However, the actual scale will depend on investor participation, market conditions, investment opportunities, and especially the support of the Vietnamese government.
 The Chief Representative of Keppel in Vietnam expressed his expectation that Keppel's global network, operational capabilities, and asset management expertise, combined with support from the Government, will contribute to the development of VIFC-HCMC to new heights, aiming to become a true financial and investment hub of the region.

Hanoi (VNA) – Vietnam is targeting economic growth of at least 10% in 2027 while maintaining macroeconomic stability and controlling inflation, heard a plenary sitting on October 30 as part of the 16th National Assembly’s second session. 
In the morning session, lawmakers discussed two draft laws: the amended Law on Real Estate Business and the amended Law on the Implementation of Grassroots Democracy. 
In the afternoon, the legislature is scheduled to debate the implementation of the 2026 socio-economic development plan and the proposed plan for 2027, as well as the implementation of the 2026 state budget, the 2027 state budget estimates and the proposed allocation of the central budget for next year. 
Other items on the agenda include the implementation of the 2026 public investment plan and the proposed public investment plan for 2027, the 2025 state budget final accounts, a review of the implementation of National Assembly Resolution No. 66/2013/QH13, dated November 29, 2013, and the completion of investment and construction of the two-lane Ho Chi Minh Road project. 
The session is being broadcast live on television and radio to enable voters and the public to follow the proceedings. 
According to a Government report, Vietnam's socio-economic performance in 2026 has achieved important and relatively comprehensive results despite complex developments in the international and regional environment, supported by concerted and decisive efforts across the political system. The country is expected to meet or exceed 14 of its 15 key socio-economic targets. 
However, the Government acknowledged that macroeconomic management and inflation control remain under considerable pressure, while deposit and lending interest rates are still high. Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) also continue to face difficulties in accessing land and credit. 
For the remaining months of 2026, the Government will focus on achieving the highest possible results against the targets set, particularly the goal of double-digit economic growth while maintaining macroeconomic stability and keeping inflation under control. 
The Government has identified 2027 as a year of acceleration and breakthrough, aimed at building the momentum, position and capacity needed to successfully implement the Resolution of the 14th National Party Congress. 
Its overarching objective is to achieve economic growth of at least 10% while maintaining macroeconomic stability, controlling inflation and safeguarding major economic balances. The Government also aims to lay the foundations for a new national development model, with science and technology, innovation and digital transformation serving as the primary drivers of growth. 
To achieve these goals, the Government will prioritise boosting economic growth in tandem with maintaining macroeconomic stability. It aims to increase state budget revenue by approximately 9.1%, strictly economise on recurrent expenditure and ensure the disbursement of 100% of allocated public investment capital. 
Further priorities include completing the institutional and legal framework, comprehensively streamlining administrative procedures, ensuring the effective operation of the two-tier local administration system and improving the quality of the civil service. Officials who shirk responsibility, avoid difficult tasks or display a reluctance to take responsibility will be promptly replaced. 
The Government will also accelerate economic restructuring and reform the growth model, promote the development of the private sector and attract foreign investment selectively, with an emphasis on technology transfer. 
The development of strategic infrastructure will be another key priority, with efforts focused on building a coordinated and modern infrastructure network, completing the expressway system and advancing major national railway projects. 
The Government will also pursue breakthroughs in science and technology, innovation and digital transformation, while ensuring the effective operation of the National Data Centre, expanding 5G coverage nationwide and piloting 6G technology. 
In education and human resource development, the focus will be on making substantive improvements in education and training quality and developing a highly skilled workforce. 
The Government will ensure that sufficient textbooks are available before the 2027-2028 academic year and complete the second phase of multi-level boarding schools for general education by August 30, 2027. 
Alongside economic development, the Government will prioritise culture, social affairs and healthcare, while strengthening social welfare and security. 
It will also consolidate national defence and security, step up foreign affairs and international integration, and make thorough preparations for the successful organisation of APEC Year 2027. 
The Government will further strengthen implementation capacity and enhance the accountability of heads of agencies and organisations, ensuring that every policy translates into tangible and measurable improvements in practice./.

articles.title: Focus capital on growth. - Vietnam.vn
articles.summary: Focus capital on growth.  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
To achieve double-digit growth targets, Dr. Can Van Luc, Chief Economist of BIDV, stated that Vietnam needs to maintain a growth rate of total social investment at approximately 13-15% per year. The total investment capital requirement is estimated at $280-300 billion per year; capital is expected to contribute about 40-42% to economic growth. Notably, the state budget is only expected to meet about 22% of the total capital requirement. The remainder must be mobilized from the domestic private sector and foreign capital sources.
Besides facing the need to mobilize large amounts of capital, the economy also has to address limitations in resource allocation and utilization. Mr. Luc analyzed that the current capital mobilization structure is unbalanced, with capital for the economy still heavily dependent on the banking system. Meanwhile, the stock market, including the stock and corporate bond markets, has not yet reached its full potential. This poses a challenge as the demand for medium and long-term investment capital is increasing, especially for infrastructure projects, industrial production, energy transformation, and technology development. If it continues to rely primarily on bank credit, the pressure on capital mobilization and maturity balance for credit institutions will increase. Therefore, solutions are needed to supplement capital for the economy, contributing to reducing pressure on the credit system and creating conditions for more appropriate resource allocation to investment needs.
Furthermore, financial expert Nguyen Thi Ngoc Ha stated that one of the limitations is the economy's heavy reliance on foreign direct investment (FDI); at the same time, domestic small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) still face many difficulties. Access to, mobilization, and utilization of resources are uneven across sectors, fields, and localities. As of the end of the third quarter of 2026, the disbursement rate of public investment only reached 62.9% of the plan. Of this, central government agencies achieved 44.1%, significantly lower than the 73.6% of localities. These figures show that allocated capital has not been injected into the economy as expected. The slow disbursement not only affects the efficiency of budget utilization but also limits the ability to create momentum for private investment and related production and business activities.
In this context, a significant amount of resources is tied up in projects facing difficulties and obstacles. According to a report by the Ministry of Finance , the Standing Agency of the Steering Committee 751 recorded 5,012 projects nationwide facing difficulties and obstacles, with a total land area of 213,581 hectares and a total investment of nearly 3.69 trillion VND. Of these, only 3,557 projects, accounting for 71% of the total number of projects and with a total investment of over 2.49 trillion VND, have been resolved and no longer face difficulties or obstacles. The remaining projects are still being handled by ministries, sectors, and localities according to their authority…
| Vietnam's capital challenge in this new growth phase lies not simply in the ability to mobilize additional resources, but also in reorganizing the capital structure and improving allocation efficiency. | 
According to expert calculations, if all approximately 5,000 stalled projects are resolved between 2026 and 2028, and about 30% of this capital is injected into the economy each year, GDP growth could increase by an additional 0.6-0.8 percentage points annually. Therefore, resolving these stalled projects is a practical solution to unlock resources and create further growth momentum in localities.
Dr. Nguyen Duc Kien, former Vice Chairman of the National Assembly 's Economic Committee, raised the issue of clarifying which obstacles can be addressed by which mechanisms. Correctly identifying the authority and responsibility of each entity is a prerequisite for the process of resolving issues to shift from proposing solutions to addressing specific difficulties in each project.
According to lawyer Pham Thanh Tuan, resolving the backlog of real estate projects requires three steps: correctly classifying the obstacles, issuing appropriate policies, and decisively implementing them at the local level. First, each locality must specifically identify where the project is stalled and what the causes are, thereby distinguishing between issues that can be proactively resolved and those requiring central government mechanisms. Banks play a role in providing capital, but can only finance projects that fully meet legal requirements. Therefore, the proactive and decisive action of local authorities in resolving procedures and obstacles within their jurisdiction directly impacts the ability to unlock investment capital. Based on this, the National Assembly, the Government , and relevant agencies can then develop solutions appropriate to each group of obstacles. Once policies have been issued, localities must promptly organize their implementation to prevent further project delays.
In addition, the development of capital mobilization channels also needs attention. Dr. Can Van Luc believes that the demand for medium and long-term investment capital is increasing, especially for infrastructure projects, industrial production, energy conversion, and technology development. Therefore, it is necessary to strongly develop the stock market, corporate bonds, and non-bank capital mobilization channels. This is not only a solution to supplement capital for the economy, but also contributes to reducing pressure on the credit system, creating conditions for more appropriate resource allocation according to investment needs.
Besides traditional fundraising channels, it is necessary to effectively utilize resources with significant potential such as green finance, remittances, tourism , trade surplus, carbon markets, land, and off-budget financial funds. For international capital, mobilization should be linked to specific, feasible projects with the capacity to absorb capital. Simultaneously, it is necessary to continue removing institutional bottlenecks, improving the quality of securities and governance in the stock market, strengthening investor protection, and developing data infrastructure. Furthermore, it is crucial to expedite tax refunds, remove obstacles related to administrative procedures and land, and create favorable conditions for projects to be implemented promptly.

articles.full_text:
Mum confronts headmaster over alleged ‘I love you’ texts to 15-year-old daughter, lunges at him as he pleads forgiveness
A video showing a mother angrily confronting a secondary school headmaster in Perak, Malaysia, has gone viral following allegations that he sent inappropriate messages to her 15-year-old daughter.
The footage, which is circulating on a popular Malaysian subreddit, shows the mother confronting the headmaster in his office, accompanied by another woman clad in a pink top.
The headmaster puts his palms together, appearing to plead for forgiveness as the mother continues to express her anger.
At one point, she hits him on the arm before lunging towards him, with the other woman stepping in to restrain her.
According to Malaysian media reports, the confrontation was reportedly sparked by allegations that the headmaster had sent the girl text messages including one that said “I love you”.
The allegations were also raised in a post on Threads, which also accused the headmaster of sexual harassment.
The Reddit thread has amassed at least 440 upvotes and 56 comments, including one that showed a certificate of the man’s appointment as headmaster.
Headmaster temporarily transferred pending investigation
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said she had directed Perak’s education department to look into the matter, according to The New Straits Times (NST).
“The headmaster involved has also been temporarily moved to the Bagan Datuk district education office pending the completion of the investigation,” she said.
Located in Perak, Bagan Datuk is about 40 kilometres away from Teluk Intan, the district where the headmaster worked in before the probe.
The viral Threads post also called on authorities to take the matter seriously and ensure students’ safety.
However, Bagan Datuk district police chief Mohamad Ali said police had not received a report about the incident, according to a Sin Chew Daily report.

In a post on Threads, Anwar urged the parties to find an immediate solution to the problem.
“This (overcrowding) happens frequently and disrupts the daily routines of many people.
“We must be more attentive and take action,” he said.
His directive followed complaints by a Threads user last night about overcrowding at train station platforms.
User @siti.anisahj posted photos of congested train platforms at the Gombak and Taipan LRT stations.
“Assalamualaikum @anwaribrahim_my. Can we ask for a few more train coaches? It is like this every day. Driving means getting stuck in traffic, while taking the train means facing overcrowding,” she said.
Anwar’s response received widespread attention, garnering nearly 37,000 likes, more than 360 comments and about 2,200 reposts as of 9.30am.
Rapid KL’s transit services have faced recurring service disruptions, passenger congestion and planned scheduling adjustments due to critical infrastructure projects and aging trains.
In February, Loke said rail operator Prasarana had ordered 26 new train sets for the Kelana Jaya LRT line.
The Kelana Jaya LRT line serves 290,000 passengers daily, making it the busiest LRT line in the Klang Valley.
